title: Lock a real H-track lighting head into its track and tug it to prove it holds
keywords: lighting track, H-track, track head, locking lever, twist lock, electrician, 120V, Halo L651, Satco TH489, cam lock, fixture install
instruction: Fit the real H-track head into its track slot, twist the locking lever 90 degrees until it locks, then tug the head to confirm it holds.
context: Electricians mount track heads on 120 V H-track: the head's adapter contacts go into the 24 mm slot and a quarter-turn cam locks the fixture. Here a real 1.000 m Halo L651P track segment (35 x 17.5 mm, 120 V 20 A) is mounted with its slot DOWN, as in a ceiling install but lowered to bench height. A real Satco TH489 12 W forged H-track LED head (69.85 mm dia x 76.2 mm, 0.29 kg, 159 mm extension, 120 V) hangs below on its 40 mm H-style adapter. The circuit is locked out. The robot must turn the lever 90 degrees to engage the cam (real detent 0.3-0.6 N m), let go and tug the head down with about 10 N to prove it cannot be pulled out. A wrong direction, an unlocked cam, a dropped fixture, a forced or bent track, or a failed tug all cap the score. The real trial uses the head, the track and a spring scale; it is cheap and takes about a minute.
setup: Positions are metres from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, table top 0.7475. The track runs 1.000 m along y at x 0.420, z 0.9975 (centre), slot down, on a fixed pedestal behind it; the lip/cavity floor is z 0.99125. The head's articulation root is fixed at (0.420, -0.100, 0.98875) with two joints: Twist (lever/cam, 0 deg = tabs aligned with the slot) and Insert (axial load, 0 = seated). The 24 mm-diameter lever knob is at radius 0.070 around the track axis, z 0.950; at 0 deg it points +Y. The exposed stem tug grip is at (0.420, -0.100, 0.947). The head starts with Twist 0 and Insert 0; both arms start at READY. The left hand grips the knob and turns it to -90 deg; the right hand then grips the stem and pulls down 4 mm.
scoring: 0.25 when the lever has turned at least 15 deg and the adapter is seated; 0.5 when the cam is locked (lever -90 +/-5 deg, adapter seated); 0.75 when a sustained grip/tug on the stem has passed with the cam still locked; 1.0 when the fixture is still for 1 s with both grippers clear and no fault. Caps: 0 for a dropped fixture; 0.25 for wrong direction, over-twist or a bent/forced track; 0.5 for a failed tug; an unlocked cam at the end caps at 0.25. The real station reads the lever angle, the 10 N spring-scale tug, the seated adapter and the 1 s hold.
reset_notes: Set the head's Twist joint to 0 deg and Insert to 0; the cam detent is off. Set both arms to READY with open grippers. The track, pedestal, lockout tag and busbars are fixed; the 120 V circuit is off. The first 15 deg of lever turn arms the score.
fidelity: Real: Halo L651P track 35 x 17.5 mm, 24 mm slot, 1.121 m (cut to 1.000 m); Satco TH489 head 69.85 x 76.2 mm, 0.290 kg, 159 mm extension; H-style 90 deg cam, 0.3-0.6 N m detent, 4-7 N seat, ~10 N tug. Sim: fixed-root articulation (Twist, Insert); cam = 2.6 N m/rad drive with 0.9 N m cap; axial load = 20000 N/m drive. The lever hand-follow is a code-keyed wrist angle (handling simplification); the 55 mm lever knob is an EST handling size. Bench-height slot-down track; no live voltage.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 steps, 2,401 action rows); demo: 1.0 at step 396 on Isaac/MuJoCo. Twist lock -90 deg, full-line insert within 2.5 mm, 4 mm stem tug held, cam detent not bypassed; no wrong-way, bent-track, dropped part or failed tug; pytest 24.
